ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A transverse simple harmonic wave propagates along the $x$-axis. The solid line represents the waveform at time $t_{1}=0$, and the dashed line represents the waveform at time $t_{2}=0.6\mathrm{s}$. The period $T$ of the particle's vibration satisfies $2T{<}0.6\mathrm{s}{<}2.5T$.

1. The speed and direction of wave propagation (calculation results are rounded to one decimal place).
2. At the moment $t=1.2s$, the displacement of the particle whose equilibrium position is at $x=1m$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is x/m, and the vertical axis is y/cm. The solid line represents the waveform at t=0, and the dashed line represents the waveform at t=0.6 s. From the figure, it can be read that the amplitude A=10 cm; the solid line has a wave crest y=10 cm at x=7 m, and has a wave trough y=-10 cm at x=3 m, so the distance between adjacent points in the same phase gives the wavelength λ=8 m. The dashed line has wave crests at x=2 m and x=10 m, and has a wave trough at x=6 m. Then reason: from t=0 to t=0.6 s, if looking at the same wave crest, the visible rightward displacement from the solid-line crest x=7 m to the dashed-line crest x=10 m is +3 m, that is, the displacement modulo λ is 3 m; if it propagates to the left, then the corresponding visible leftward displacement can be taken as 5 m. The problem gives 2T<0.6 s<2.5T, so within 0.6 s the distance propagated by the wave should satisfy 2λ<d<2.5λ, that is, 16 m<d<20 m. If it propagates along the +x direction, the actual propagation distance is congruent to 3 m modulo 8 m, and in this range is d=2λ+3=19 m, satisfying the condition; if it propagates along the -x direction, the distance is congruent to 5 m modulo 8 m, and nearby it is 13 m or 21 m, neither of which is between 16 m and 20 m. Therefore the wave propagates along the +x direction, and the speed v=d/Δt=19/0.6=31.666... m/s, rounded to 31.7 m/s. When t=1.2 s, it is twice 0.6 s, and the total rightward displacement of the wave along +x is 2×19=38 m. For a right-traveling wave, y(x,t)=y0(x-vt), so the displacement at x=1 m is equal to the displacement of the initial waveform at x=1-38=-37 m. Using the periodicity λ=8 m, -37 m is in the same phase as 3 m, so y(1,1.2 s)=y0(3 m). In the figure, the solid line is at a wave trough at x=3 m, and the displacement is -10 cm.
